explanation:
[EFFECT]
Clear weather gives a small boost to predicted hourly rentals, while mist or cloud cover has almost no effect compared to clear skies. Light rain or snow causes the largest single drop in demand — reducing it by roughly a third in multiplicative terms. Heavy rain also strongly suppresses demand, though the model places it very slightly above light rain/snow, meaning the steepest penalty falls at "light rain/snow" rather than at the most severe category.

[IMPORTANCE]
Weather situation ranks 6th out of 9 features in overall importance, making it a below-average driver of predicted demand in this model. Hour of day, temperature, and year, among others, have a greater influence on hourly rentals than weather conditions alone.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Since the sharpest demand drop occurs at light rain or snow (category 3), consider pre-emptively reducing bike redistribution effort and staffing during forecasts of even moderate precipitation — there is little operational benefit in maintaining full availability when conditions reach that threshold.
